📺 Black-ish (2014–2022)

Black-ish follows Andre “Dre” Johnson, a successful advertising executive who enjoys a comfortable life with his wife, Rainbow, and their children in an affluent Los Angeles neighborhood. Despite his professional success, Dre worries that his family is losing touch with their cultural identity and traditions. Determined to keep his children connected to their roots, he frequently introduces unconventional parenting lessons that lead to hilarious misunderstandings, family arguments, and unforgettable moments. Alongside his intelligent and outspoken wife, Dre navigates marriage, career challenges, raising children, and the complicated expectations of modern family life. Through clever humor, emotional storytelling, and relatable experiences, Black-ish explores family, identity, race, relationships, parenting, and the importance of embracing where you come from.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Family • Sitcom

⭐ IMDb: 7.3/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 22 minutes per episode • TV-14

🎥 Creator: Kenya Barris

🏆 Awards: Winner of multiple NAACP Image Awards and a Primetime Emmy Award.

📺 Where to Watch: Hulu and Disney+ in the United States, depending on subscription availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Black-ish (stylized as black·ish) is an American sitcom television series created by Kenya Barris. It aired on ABC from September 24, 2014, to April 19, 2022, running for eight seasons with 175 episodes. Black-ish follows an upper class well-off Black family headed by Andre "Dre" Johnson, a successful advertising executive (Anthony Anderson), and his wife Rainbow "Bow", an anesthesiologist (Tracee Ellis Ross). The show revolves around the wealthy Johnson family as they juggle personal, familial and sociopolitical issues, particularly in trying to reconcile their desire to stay true to their Black identities with their choice to live in a wealthy, suburban white neighborhood.
